title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland Established
note: Federation established 1 August 1953 under UK Rhodesia and Nyasaland Federation Act. Description accurately notes white settler dominance and African nationalist opposition.

title: African National Congress of Southern Rhodesia Founded
note: SRANC formed 12 September 1957 by amalgamation of Salisbury Youth League and Bulawayo ANC branch; Joshua Nkomo elected president. Description correct.

title: State of Emergency and ANC Banned
note: State of emergency declared 29 February 1959 by Whitehead government; SRANC banned under Unlawful Organizations Act; ~500 arrested. All core facts correct.

title: ZAPU Founded by Joshua Nkomo
note: ZAPU formed 17 December 1961 after the NDP was banned. Founded by Nkomo alongside Sithole, Mugabe, and others. Soviet alignment and Ndebele support noted in sources.

title: ZANU Splits from ZAPU
note: ZANU founded August 1963 by Ndabaningi Sithole and others (Mugabe as secretary-general). Split reasons (Nkomo leadership style, external vs internal struggle) confirmed. Broad ethnic dimension (Shona/ZANU, Ndebele/ZAPU) documented.

title: Central African Federation Dissolved
note: Federation dissolved 31 December 1963. Northern Rhodesia became Zambia (Oct 1964) and Nyasaland became Malawi (July 1964). Southern Rhodesia reverted to colonial status. All facts correct.

title: Mugabe Imprisoned
note: Mugabe arrested December 1963, sentenced March 1964 for subversive speech; detained ~10 years, released November 1974. Earned law degrees by correspondence — confirmed. Description says 'eleven-year detention' but actual figure is closer to 10 years; minor discrepancy.

title: Ian Smith's Unilateral Declaration of Independence
note: UDI declared 11 November 1965 at 11:00 local time on Armistice Day. First unilateral break from UK since American colonies. Britain declared it illegal, declined military force. All facts correct.

title: UN Security Council Imposes Mandatory Sanctions
note: Resolution 232 adopted 16 December 1966 imposing mandatory comprehensive economic sanctions including tobacco, chrome, asbestos. Vote 11-0 with 4 abstentions. Description says 'first time UN imposed compulsory sanctions on any state' — confirmed by SIPRI. South Africa and Portugal sanctions-busting confirmed.

title: Battle of Sinoia — First ZANU Guerrilla Attack
note: 28 April 1966, seven ZANLA combatants engaged Rhodesian police at Sinoia; all killed. Commemorated as Chimurenga Day. Described as ZANU insurgents (technically ZANLA wing) — correct. Number of combatants (seven) confirmed.

title: Rhodesia Declares Itself a Republic
note: Referendum held 20 June 1969 approved republican status. However, Rhodesia formally declared itself a republic on 2 March 1970, NOT in 1969. The event year should be 1970. Year attribution is incorrect.

title: ZANLA Launches Northeast Offensive
note: ZANLA's attack on Altena Farm in Centenary district in December 1972 opened a new sustained phase of guerrilla war from Mozambican/Zambian bases using Maoist tactics. Northeast focus and Mozambican/Zambian bases confirmed.

title: Lusaka Accord and Detente
note: Lusaka Unity Accord signed 7 December 1974. South African pressure on Smith to release detainees including Mugabe and brief ceasefire confirmed. Frontline states involvement (Zambia, Mozambique, Botswana, South Africa) confirmed. Detente ultimately failed — correct.

title: Mozambican Independence Transforms the War
note: Mozambique independence 25 June 1975 under FRELIMO. Gave ZANLA secure bases along entire eastern border; Rhodesia lacked manpower to defend 1,300km frontier. All claims confirmed.

title: Geneva Conference on Rhodesia Fails
note: Geneva Conference opened October 1976 with Smith government, ZANU, ZAPU, internal leaders under British chair. ZAPU+ZANU attended as Patriotic Front. Conference adjourned 14 December 1976 without agreement. All claims confirmed.

title: Mugabe Becomes ZANU Leader and PATRIOTIC FRONT Forms
note: Mugabe consolidated ZANU leadership in 1976 after split from Sithole; Patriotic Front formed as ZANU-ZAPU tactical alliance for Geneva negotiations. Separate military commands maintained. All facts confirmed.

title: Rhodesian Forces Strike Mozambique — Chimoio and Tembue Raids
note: Operation Dingo 23-25 November 1977. Attacked ~10,000 ZANLA at Chimoio and ~4,000 at Tembué. Death toll over 1,000. Description says 'hundreds to thousands' — consistent with sources. International outrage confirmed.

title: Internal Settlement — Muzorewa Heads Transitional Government
note: Internal Settlement signed 3 March 1978 between Smith, Muzorewa, Sithole, and Chirau. Muzorewa became PM under Zimbabwe Rhodesia in 1979. Rejected by PF and international community. All claims confirmed.

title: Lancaster House Agreement
note: Agreement signed 21 December 1979, ending Bush War with ceasefire framework, elections under British supervision, constitutional protection of white seats (10 years) and property rights. All claims confirmed.

title: Zimbabwe Independence — Mugabe Becomes Prime Minister
note: Independence 18 April 1980. Elections February 1980; ZANU-PF won 57 of 80 common roll seats. Mugabe sworn in as PM. Conciliatory inaugural address confirmed. Claim of 'surprising Western observers' is consistent with historical accounts.

title: Reconciliation Policy Announced
note: Reconciliation policy widely documented — white civil servants, security officers, and farm owners retained. Prevented white exodus, maintained economic functioning. Critics noting deferred land issue — confirmed in historical literature.

title: Entumbane Clashes between ZANLA and ZIPRA
note: Entumbane I (November 1980) and Entumbane II (February 1981) both documented. Event dated 1981 but initial clashes were November 1980; the major uprising was February 1981. Description mixing both incidents — core facts correct, year is technically the 1981 uprising.

title: Nkomo Dismissed — Gukurahundi Begins
note: Nkomo dismissed 1982 following alleged arms cache discovery on ZAPU properties. North Korean-trained Fifth Brigade deployed to Matabeleland. Fifth Brigade outside normal military command confirmed. All facts correct.

title: Gukurahundi Massacres in Matabeleland
note: Fifth Brigade deployed January 1983. Death toll: Catholic Commission confirmed minimum 2,750-8,000; IAGS estimate 20,000; locals cite 20,000-40,000. Description's '20,000 civilians' uses the widely cited estimate. Methods (executions, food blockades, burning villages) confirmed. Catholic Commission report suppressed until 1997 — confirmed.

title: ZANU-PF Wins Elections Amid Violence
note: 1985 elections held June-July; ZANU-PF increased majority to 64 seats. Widespread violence against ZAPU supporters in Matabeleland confirmed. International observers noted intimidation. Results confirmed. Note: ZAPU still won all 15 Matabeleland seats despite the violence.

title: Unity Accord — ZANU-PF Absorbs ZAPU
note: Unity Accord signed 22 December 1987 merging ZAPU into ZANU-PF. Ended Gukurahundi. De facto one-party state created with 99 of 100 parliamentary seats. Executive presidency created simultaneously. All facts correct.

title: Mugabe Becomes Executive President
note: Mugabe became Zimbabwe's first executive president on 31 December 1987, abolishing the Prime Minister role. Combined head of state and government powers. Constitutional amendments described are accurate.

title: One-Party State Attempt Abandoned
note: One-party state plans abandoned in 1990 under public opposition and donor/international pressure. Formal multipartyism returned. ZANU-PF retained de facto hegemony via state resources and patronage. All claims supported by sources.

title: War Veterans Compensation Crisis
note: Mugabe capitulated to war veterans' demands for unbudgeted gratuities (Z$50,000 per veteran). Currency collapsed ~72% on 14 November 1997 ('Black Friday'). Event marks start of economic implosion. Description's 'Z$50,000 per veteran' confirmed. Month (November) and percent collapse confirmed.

title: Gukurahundi Report Published — Catholic Commission
note: Report 'Breaking the Silence, Building True Peace' published 1997 jointly by Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace and Legal Resources Foundation. Based on 1,000+ eyewitness accounts. Government refused accountability. Confirmed as definitive primary source.

title: Food Riots in Harare
note: January 1998 urban food riots over maize meal price increases confirmed. Army deployed; nine reportedly killed; ~800 arrested. Brief price freeze and arrests of ringleaders confirmed. IMF-linked subsidy removal as contributing factor supported.

title: Zimbabwe Enters Second Congo War
note: Zimbabwe deployed forces to DRC August 1998 alongside Namibia and Angola supporting Kabila. 6,000 troops with tanks and MiGs. Cost ~£1m/day. Mining concessions for elites confirmed. Three SADC states intervening confirmed.

title: MDC Founded
note: MDC founded at mass rally 11 September 1999 in Harare. Led by Morgan Tsvangirai, drawn from Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions and civic society. Founded to contest Mugabe/ZANU-PF. Note: The curated JSON has no 1999 MDC event but references it under the 2000 referendum entry — filing as inferred event verified.

title: Constitutional Referendum Defeat
note: Referendum 12-13 February 2000; proposed constitution rejected 55% to 45% (697,754 No to 578,000 Yes). First national vote Mugabe lost. MDC led No campaign. ZANU-PF accelerated land seizures and suppression in response. All facts correct.

title: Fast-Track Land Reform — Farm Invasions Begin
note: War veterans with state backing began occupying white-owned farms from early 2000 after referendum defeat. ~4,000 white farmers displaced; ~1 million farm workers affected. Tobacco production fell ~75% within five years. All figures and claims consistent with sources.

title: Parliamentary Elections — MDC Wins 57 Seats
note: June 2000 elections: MDC won 57 of 120 elected seats with 47% of vote; ZANU-PF won 62 with 48%. Widespread violence and fraud documented by international observers. All claims confirmed.

title: Zimbabwe Suspended from IMF Programs
note: Zimbabwe incurred IMF arrears February 2001; declared ineligible for general resources 24 September 2001. Multilateral and donor aid withdrawal followed. All core claims confirmed. Description says 'suspended 2001' — technically correct per IMF records.

title: Presidential Election — Mugabe Re-elected Amid Violence and Fraud
note: March 2002 election; Mugabe won 56.2%. EU observers prevented from monitoring. Systematic ballot stuffing, urban disenfranchisement, violence against MDC supporters documented. AU acknowledged irregularities. EU/Commonwealth declared it failed democratic standards. All confirmed.

title: EU and Commonwealth Sanctions Imposed
note: EU imposed targeted sanctions (travel bans, asset freezes) on Mugabe and ruling elite. Commonwealth suspended Zimbabwe. Description says Zimbabwe 'withdrew from Commonwealth 2003' — it was suspended 2002, then withdrew 2003. Minor clarification but not a factual error in this event.

title: Zimbabwe Withdraws from the Commonwealth
note: Zimbabwe formally withdrew 7 December 2003 after indefinite suspension upheld by CHOGM Nigeria (6-1 vote, South Africa dissenting). Only third voluntary withdrawal in Commonwealth history. All claims confirmed.

title: Hyperinflation Begins to Accelerate
note: Annual inflation reached 624% in 2004. Price controls caused shortages. Money printing to finance deficits from war veterans, DRC spending, farm seizures confirmed. Self-reinforcing spiral description is accurate.

title: Operation Murambatsvina Destroys Urban Communities
note: Operation launched 19 May 2005. UN estimates: 700,000 directly displaced, up to 2.4 million indirectly affected. UN Special Envoy condemned as violating international humanitarian law. Political targeting of MDC urban areas confirmed. All claims correct.

title: Reserve Bank Redenominates — First Zimbabwe Dollar Reissued
note: First redenomination 1 August 2006 (Operation Sunrise): three zeros removed, exchange rate 1000:1. Governor Gono stated inflation near 1,200% at the time. Savings destroyed by inflation confirmed. Cosmetic measure description accurate.

title: MDC Leaders Beaten in Police Custody
note: March 11 2007: 50+ opposition leaders arrested heading to prayer meeting at Zimbabwe Grounds, Highfields. Tsvangirai, Mutambara, Biti, and others beaten in custody. Tsvangirai suffered head injury. International condemnation confirmed. Description mentions 'Tendai Biti and movement figures' — Biti was among those detained and beaten, confirmed.

title: March Elections — MDC Wins Parliament, Runoff Needed for Presidency
note: March 2008 harmonized elections: MDC won parliamentary majority (109 of 210 seats). Tsvangirai won 47.87% of presidential votes vs Mugabe 43.24% — below 50% threshold for outright win. ZANU-PF delayed results weeks. All facts confirmed.

title: Pre-Runoff Political Violence — Operation Makavhoterapapi
note: Operation 'Where Did You Vote?' documented by HRW; killed 200+ MDC activists, tortured thousands, displaced tens of thousands. State-organized, targeted MDC rural districts. Tsvangirai withdrew 22 June 2008 citing impossibility of free campaign. All claims confirmed.

title: Hyperinflation Reaches 89.7 Sextillion Percent
note: Peak inflation November 2008: officially estimated at 89.7 sextillion percent (89,700,000,000,000,000,000,000%). Second-worst hyperinflation in history after Hungary 1946. Prices doubled multiple times per day. Informal dollarization confirmed. All claims correct.

title: Cholera Epidemic Kills Thousands
note: Cholera outbreak 2008-2009: 98,585 cases, 4,287 deaths — exceeds event's 'over 4,000 deaths and nearly 100,000 infected' which is accurate. Water infrastructure collapse documented. Mugabe's denial confirmed. All claims verified.

title: Zimbabwe Dollar Abandoned — Multi-Currency System Adopted
note: Foreign currency use legalized 29 January 2009; Zimbabwe dollar formally abandoned April 2009. Dollarization ended hyperinflation immediately. Loss of savings from prior inflation confirmed. All claims correct.

title: Government of National Unity Formed
note: GNU formed 13 February 2009 (Global Political Agreement signed September 2008, implemented February 2009). Tsvangirai as PM, Mugabe retained presidency. MDC gained economic ministries; ZANU-PF kept security. All claims confirmed.

title: Economic Recovery Under GNU
note: GDP grew 8-9% annually 2009-2012. 2011 specifically saw high growth. Recovery described as fragile and commodity-driven — consistent with World Bank analysis. Basic services partially resumed. All claims confirmed.

title: New Constitution Adopted by Referendum
note: Referendum 16-17 March 2013; approved by 94.5% of voters (event says 95% — close rounding). Presidential term limits (two five-year terms), devolved senate, bill of rights, gender quotas confirmed. Term limits not applying retroactively to Mugabe confirmed. All facts correct.

title: Mugabe Re-elected — MDC Alleges Massive Fraud
note: July 2013: Mugabe won 61% vs Tsvangirai ~34%. MDC alleged voters' roll discrepancies, urban voter exclusion, security force structural advantage. Constitutional Court upheld result. Power-sharing ended. All claims confirmed.

title: Grace Mugabe Rises to Power — Joice Mujuru Purged
note: Grace Mugabe led campaign against Mujuru with corruption/treachery allegations at December 2014 ZANU-PF congress. Mujuru dismissed 8 December 2014. Mujuru was liberation war hero. Factional conflict (G40 vs Lacoste) confirmed as accelerating 2017 coup. All claims accurate.

title: Cash Shortages Begin — Surrogate Bond Notes Introduced
note: Cash shortages began 2015-2016 but bond notes were not introduced until November 2016, not 2015. The event year is off by one year for the bond note introduction. Cash shortage beginning in 2015 is accurate; bond notes are a 2016 event.

title: Anti-Government Protests — #ThisFlag Movement
note: Pastor Evan Mawarire started #ThisFlag April 2016. July 6 stay-away shut down Harare businesses. Mawarire arrested then released under public pressure. New limits on state impunity in social media age confirmed. All claims correct.

title: Military Coup Removes Mugabe After 37 Years
note: ZDF seized broadcaster and placed Mugabe under house arrest 15 November 2017 (tanks moved night of 14-15 November). Framed as targeting 'criminals around him' (G40/Grace). Triggered by Mnangagwa's 6 November firing. Mugabe resigned 21 November after impeachment proceedings. All dates and facts confirmed.

title: Mnangagwa Becomes President
note: Mnangagwa sworn in 24 November 2017 at National Sports Stadium before ~60,000. 'Open Zimbabwe for business' rhetoric confirmed. Personal implication in Gukurahundi atrocities and retention of deep state apparatus confirmed in historical literature. All claims accurate.

title: First Post-Mugabe Election — Mnangagwa Wins Narrowly
note: July 30 2018 elections: Mnangagwa won 50.8% — just above threshold to avoid runoff. ZANU-PF won two-thirds parliamentary majority. Chamisa/MDC Alliance alleged fraud, filed court challenge (dismissed). Mixed international observer assessments confirmed. All facts correct.

title: Post-Election Crackdown — Military Kills Six Protesters
note: 1 August 2018: military deployed armored vehicles into Harare, opened fire on protesters near ZEC offices; six killed, dozens injured. Motlanthe commission found shootings unjustified. All claims confirmed.

title: Currency Reintroduction and Economic Crisis
note: RTGS dollar introduced February 2019; June 2019 mandate as sole legal tender. Rapid depreciation and loss of confidence confirmed. Annual inflation above 500% by December 2019 confirmed. All claims accurate.

title: Fuel Price Protests — January 2019 Crackdown
note: Fuel price hike ~130% announced 12 January 2019. Nationwide shutdown. Security forces killed at least 12-17 people (sources vary 8-17). Door-to-door raids, torture documented by Amnesty/HRW. Internet shutdown confirmed. ZCTU-led shutdown confirmed. All claims consistent.

title: Cyclone Idai Devastates Eastern Zimbabwe
note: Cyclone Idai struck March 2019; ~340 deaths in Zimbabwe, mainly Chimanimani and Chipinge districts. ~270,000 affected, ~51,000 displaced. Flash floods and landslides confirmed. All claims accurate.

title: Journalist Hopewell Chin'ono Arrested Amid COVID Crackdown
note: Chin'ono arrested 20 July 2020 for incitement after exposing COVID PPE procurement fraud (linked to Mnangagwa's son). 44 days pre-trial detention. Arrested alongside Job Sikhala (opposition MP) — confirmed. Global press freedom symbol. All claims accurate.

title: COVID-19 and Economic Deterioration
note: COVID-19 compounded pre-existing economic crisis; informal economy (80%+ of livelihoods) devastated by lockdowns. Inflation above 700% for much of 2020 confirmed. Sinopharm vaccine dependency on Chinese donations is accurate per available reporting.

title: Kariba Reservoir Falls to Critical Levels
note: Low Kariba levels causing severe load-shedding documented across 2019-2022 period. Load-shedding of 18+ hours per day confirmed for peak drought periods. Kariba as ~40% of Zimbabwe's electricity confirmed. Under-investment in alternative generation confirmed. Year (2021) plausible for a severe drought episode.

title: Gold Mafia and Illicit Mining Exposed
note: Al Jazeera's Gold Mafia investigation was published in March-April 2023, not 2021. The event year is incorrect. The underlying facts (gold smuggling, military/ZANU-PF connections, senior officials involved, $1.5B estimate) are confirmed for 2023.

title: Lithium Mining Boom — Chinese Investment Surge
note: Chinese firms acquired Bikita Minerals (Sinomine, $180M) and Arcadia Lithium (Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, $422M) in 2021-2022. Export ban on raw lithium ore confirmed. Chinese investment >$1.4B in two years, 90% of mining capacity confirmed. Environmental oversight concerns noted in sources. All claims accurate.

title: SADC Election Observer Mission Condemns August Election
note: August 2023 elections: Mnangagwa won 52.6% vs Chamisa 44%. SADC observer mission issued unprecedented critical report. Mission head Mumba later called elections 'most fraudulent in SADC history'. All claims confirmed including specific percentage.

title: Opposition MPs and Activists Jailed
note: Post-election wave of arrests against CCC members, opposition MPs, and civil society confirmed. Job Sikhala's extended pre-trial detention (over a year) documented. Formal opposition structure dismantled. All claims confirmed.

title: Nelson Chamisa Resigns as CCC Leader
note: Chamisa resigned/announced departure 27 January 2024, not December 2023 as stated. The ZANU-PF infiltration through Sengezo Tshabangu and fake CCC appointments is confirmed, but the resignation date is incorrect (2024, not 2023).

title: Zimbabwe Gold (ZiG) Currency Launched
note: ZiG launched 8 April 2024, backed by gold and foreign exchange reserves. Initial rate 13.56 ZiG per USD confirmed (description says replaced ZWL at 13.56 — accurate). Within months ZiG depreciated significantly and parallel market diverged. All claims correct.

title: El Nino Drought — Food Emergency Declared
note: Mnangagwa declared national disaster April 2024 due to El Nino drought. Appealed for $2 billion in international assistance confirmed. Maize production fell sharply; 2.7-6 million people food insecure (description's 7 million is at the high end of estimates but within range of projections). All core claims confirmed.

title: Kariba Power Crisis Deepens
note: Lake Kariba fell to ~4.5% live storage October 2024. Load-shedding exceeded 12-20 hours per day in Zimbabwe during 2024 crisis. Crippled industry and agriculture. Long-term under-investment in alternative generation confirmed. All claims accurate.
